tech.name: Stateless MCP (Model Context Protocol, spec 2026-07-28)
tech.status: shipped: 2026-07-28 is the current MCP protocol version
tech.one_line: MCP drops the initialize handshake and the session ID: every request carries what it needs, so any server instance can answer it.

predecessor.name: Session-based MCP (spec 2025-11-25): initialize handshake and Mcp-Session-Id

hook.text: MCP before July 28, 2026: your server quit, you lost your order; now any server takes it, but how, and why, in 60 seconds?

claims.text: In stateful (pre-2026-07-28) MCP, if the server instance handling a client session fails, that session state is lost and the client must reconnect and redo the handshake.
The 2026-07-28 specification was released on July 28, 2026.
Under 2026-07-28, any request can land on any server instance behind a plain round-robin load balancer.

before.text: Here's how, in one diner. Your AI app is the customer; an MCP server is the waiter bringing its tools. Old MCP: shake hands, maybe get a table number, a session ID, and your order lives in his head. Other waiters: not my table.

claims.text: MCP is an open protocol connecting LLM applications to external data sources and tools.
In 2025-11-25 the initialize request and initialized notification must be the first interaction between client and server.
In 2025-11-25 a Streamable HTTP server MAY assign a session ID at initialization in the MCP-Session-Id header; clients MUST then include it on all later requests.
Session state lives on one server instance: a plain round-robin load balancer would route requests to servers without that state, so operators use sticky sessions.

new.text: The new MCP drops both. Every request is now a complete order slip, so any waiter can take it. Need a basket kept? The server hands back a ticket; your AI shows it next time.

claims.text: 2026-07-28 removes the initialize/initialized handshake; every request carries its protocol version and client capabilities in _meta (SEP-2575).
2026-07-28 removes protocol-level sessions and the Mcp-Session-Id header from Streamable HTTP (SEP-2567).
Stateless by default: any request can be handled by any server instance.
Servers that need cross-call state mint an explicit handle from a tool (create_basket() returns basket_id) and the model threads it through later calls as an ordinary argument.

why.text: For you, AI tools can stop hanging on one machine: busy day, add servers; one quits, the next takes your next order. And the ticket stays in your chat for tomorrow.

claims.text: Any request can now land on any server instance behind a plain round-robin load balancer without needing shared storage.
Stateless by default enables straightforward horizontal scaling and improves resilience, as any request can be handled by any server instance.

Handles appear in tool results and so in the chat transcript; clients that persist chats (most) persist them, and reopening a conversation after a restart, a reload or on another device puts the handle back in front of the model.

takeaway.text: How? The order moved onto the slip. Why? Any waiter can take it. That's stateless: a server that remembers nothing is a server anyone can replace.

claims.text: Every request is self-contained (version and capabilities per request), so any server instance can handle it.
The protocol no longer manages session state; applications that need state carry it in explicit handles.

outro.text: Spoken call to action: subscribe for the next one. On screen: the takeaway card and a Subscribe button. No 'Next' line: the next episode is not decided.

edges.label: 1 handshake, 2 session ID, then every request
